'''Michael Miles Gore''' {{post-nominals|country=AUS|size=100%|AO}} (5 September 1934 – 8 January 2022) was a British-born Australian engineer, physicist, and science explainer, who worked at the [[Australian National University]] in [[Canberra]]. He was noted for being the founder of [[Questacon]], the first interactive science centre in Australia.

==Early life==
Gore was born in [[Bolton]], [[Lancashire]], on 5 September 1934.<ref name=ANUoral>{{cite web | url=http://www.anu.edu.au/emeritus/ohp/interviews/michael_gore.html | title=Interview with Professor Michael Gore AM | first=Pater | last=Stewart | publisher=Emeritus Faculty Oral History, Australian National University | date=June 2014 | access-date=17 January 2019 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190606125417/http://www.anu.edu.au/emeritus/ohp/interviews/michael_gore.html | archive-date=6 June 2019 | url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |title=Who's Who in Australia 2009 |date=2007 |publisher=Crown Content |pages=857 |isbn=9781740951661 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=5es-AQAAIAAJ&q=Michael+Miles+Gore+1934 |access-date=8 January 2022}}</ref> He was the only child of May Robinson and Ernest Gore, who worked as an [[electrical engineer]].<ref name=Lindell>{{cite news|title=Questacon founder Professor Mike Gore dies|url=https://www.canberratimes.com.au/story/7574136/questacon-founder-professor-mike-gore-dies/|first=Jasper|last=Lindell|date=8 January 2022|access-date=8 January 2022|newspaper=The Canberra Times}}</ref> Gore attended Worsley Technical School for two years, before completing his secondary education at Bolton Senior Tech.<ref name="Libraries ACT">{{cite web|title=Michael Gore – Canberra Citizen of the Year: 1983|date=10 January 2021|url=https://www.library.act.gov.au/find/history/frequentlyaskedquestions/personal_stories/canberra-citizen-of-the-year-1967/michael-gore|access-date=8 January 2022|publisher=Libraries ACT|location=Canberra|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220109010411/https://www.library.act.gov.au/find/history/frequentlyaskedquestions/personal_stories/canberra-citizen-of-the-year-1967/michael-gore|archivedate=9 January 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> He first graduated with a [[Bachelor of Science]] in electrical engineering.<ref name="ANU" /> He subsequently undertook [[Postgraduate education|postgraduate studies]] in that field at [[Leeds University]], obtaining a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] in the 1950s.<ref name="CT-AO">[https://www.canberratimes.com.au/act-news/questacon-founder-dr-mike-gore-appointed-an-officer-in-the-order-of-australia-20150125-12vspb.html Questacon founder Dr Mike Gore appointed an officer in the Order of Australia], Clare Colley, [[Canberra Times]], 26 January 2015</ref>

==Professional career==
At the conclusion of his studies, Gore was offered a post-doctoral position at [[Brown University]] for nine months, as well as the position of lecturer in [[physics]] at the [[Australian National University]] (ANU) in [[Canberra]].<ref name="Libraries ACT"/> He accepted both positions after arranging a deferral of the starting date of the latter,<ref name="Libraries ACT"/> and consequently immigrated to Australia in 1962.<ref name=ANU>{{cite web|title=Honorary Professor Mike Gore AO|url=https://cpas.anu.edu.au/people/academics/honorary-professor-mike-gore-ao|access-date=8 January 2022|publisher=Australian National University|location=Canberra|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220109000724/https://cpas.anu.edu.au/people/academics/honorary-professor-mike-gore-ao|archivedate=9 January 2022|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="ABC obit">{{cite news|title=Professor Michael Gore AO, founder of national science institution Questacon, dies in Canberra|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2022-01-08/professor-michael-gore-questacon-founder-dies/100745450|first=Kate|last=Midena|date=8 January 2022|access-date=8 January 2022|publisher=Australian Broadcasting Corporation}}</ref> Gore was appointed Acting Warden of Burton Hall in 1973 and served as Warden of Garran Hall in 1974-1975<ref name=ANUoral />

He later became a Professor, and in 1987 left the ANU and was later styled Professor Emeritus. As at early 2015, Gore was a Sessional Lecturer at the ANU, based at the Centre for the Public Awareness of Science.<ref name="ANU" />

===Explaining science===
Gore established [[Questacon]], the national science centre, in Canberra in 1980. It was the first interactive science centre in the country.<ref name="ANU" /> It was originally based in the recently shuttered, historic [[Braddon, Australian Capital Territory#Ainslie School|Ainslie Public School]] (built 1927). He was inspired to set up the centre after visiting the [[Exploratorium]] in [[San Francisco]] in 1976. Questacon moved to the permanent building on [[Lake Burley Griffin]] in 1988, after Gore left academia the year before to become the foundation director of Questacon – The National Science and Technology Centre.<ref name="CT-AO" /><ref name="ANU" /><ref>[http://www.questacon.edu.au/history/timeline.html Questacon timeline], [[Questacon]], accessed 26 January 2015</ref> He retired back to academia in 1999, working as an [[adjunct professor]] in science communication.<ref name="ANU" />

Gore was a scientific advisor to the [[Australian Broadcasting Corporation|ABC]] television series "[[Towards 2000]]". He established the ANU's Centre for the Public Awareness of Science (CPAS) in 1995.<ref name="CT-AO" /> In 2010, Gore was a founding member of The Faraday Club, established by Dr Howie Firth, {{post-nominals|country=GBR|MBE}}, of the [[Orkney International Science Festival]], to recognise science communicators of international standing and named after [[Michael Faraday]], leading English scientist of the nineteenth century.<ref>{{cite web|title=The Faraday Club|url=http://faradayclubaward.org/|website=The Faraday Club|accessdate=13 January 2018}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Gore was married to Joyce Klaber.<ref name=Lindell/> They met during his time in the United States as a post-doctoral research fellow at [[Brown University]], where she was studying US History.<ref>Conversation with Joyce Gore, 25 October 2022.</ref><ref name="Libraries ACT"/><ref name="ABC obit"/> They had three children.<ref name="ABC obit"/>

Gore died on 8 January 2022, in [[Canberra]]. He was 87 years old.<ref name=Lindell/><ref name="ABC obit"/>

* 'Canberran of the Year'<ref name=Lindell/><ref name="Libraries ACT"/><ref name="ANU" />
* [[Churchill Fellowship]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Michael M Gore - Churchill Trust |url=https://www.churchilltrust.com.au/fellow/michael-gore-act-1983/ |website=www.churchilltrust.com.au |access-date=16 April 2021 |language=en-AU}}</ref>
; 1986
* Member of the [[Order of Australia]] (AM) in recognition of service to scientific education.<ref>{{cite web|title=Michael Miles Gore AM|url=https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/881034|publisher=[[Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet (Australia)|Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet]]|date=26 January 1986|accessdate=26 January 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220108225053/https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/881034|archive-date=8 January 2022|url-status=live}}</ref>
; 1992
* [[Eureka Prize]] – Gore and Questacon<ref name="ANU" />
; 2001
* Award for Outstanding Service to Physics in Australia ([[Australian Institute of Physics]])<ref>[http://www.aip.org.au/info/?q=content/award-outstanding-service-physics-australia Award for Outstanding Service to Physics in Australia], [[Australian Institute of Physics]], accessed 26 January 2015</ref>
; 2006
* Academy Medal, [[Australian Academy of Science]]<ref>[https://www.science.org.au/awardees-2006 Awardees for 2006] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150128120630/https://www.science.org.au/awardees-2006 |date=28 January 2015 }}, [[Australian Academy of Science]], 2006, accessed 26 January 2015</ref>
; 2015
* Officer of the Order of Australia (AO) for distinguished service to science through a range of public outreach, communication and education initiatives on a national and international level, and as a mentor and role model for young scientists.<ref>{{cite web|title=Officer (AO) of the Order of Australia in the General Division|url=http://www.gg.gov.au/sites/default/files/files/honours/ad/ad2015/Media%20Notes%20-%20AO.pdf|page=[http://www.gg.gov.au/sites/default/files/files/honours/ad/ad2015/Media%20Notes%20-%20AO.pdf#page=14 14]|publisher=[[Official Secretary to the Governor-General of Australia]]|date=26 January 2015|accessdate=26 January 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190323124336/http://gg.gov.au/sites/default/files/files/honours/ad/ad2015/Media%20Notes%20-%20AO.pdf|archive-date=23 March 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref>
